full_judgment: "But a remand order is not to be granted as a matter of routine. Section 29 All 184 P.C. and 17 All 112 P.C. Mr. Moksudur Rahman found it difficult to pinpoint the area of investigation which could be done on remand. The crucial question is as to the physical presence of the vendor. It is presumed under section 60 that the registration was done in accordance with law and the requirement of the law was fulfilled. It is a rebuttable presumption, no doubt, but Mr. Moksudur Rahman could not argue, how the evidence as it is, has rebutted the presumption. The defendants got ample opportunity at the trial stage and no such rebuttal evidence was adduced. Hence the prayer for remand does not merit consideration. Since the point has been settled already on which the leave was granted, Mr. Ahmed is correct in saying the appeal has become of mere academic interest."
